column1: Table. Ecological data per plot. This table shows the species, type (Snag or Log), number and girth of the trees present in each plot. Where the field is empty, the number of corresponding trees is 0. Only girth categories with at least one occurrence are shown. Trees were considered snags when they were standing, but had obviously been lacking bark for a long time. If a tree had fallen and looked as if it had lost its bark long time ago, it was considered a Log. Standing or fallen trees with bark or with recent bark loss were categorized as "normal" trees, as they did not represent a significantly different substrate for the observed lichen flora.
